PullRequest.Title: remove migration hint on response
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The migration hint assessment was placed in every eligible chat request's pre-invocation Promise.all. In Always mode it repeated collection-wide prompt discovery and harness/MCP migration assessment per request; even when prompt-location caches were warm, the request still awaited source-folder/session readiness and optional MCP assessment before sending the message to the agent.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Eligible agent-host messages could not reach invokeAgent until migration assessment completed, adding cold filesystem discovery and potentially a bounded protocol-readiness wait or MCP file reads to time-to-response on every request in Always mode (or the first request of each session in Once mode).
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Agent-host requests now await only hook and automatic-instruction collection in Step 2; migration-hint discovery, source-folder waits, and optional MCP planning are no longer performed before agent invocation for each eligible response.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The deleted LEFT line 1781 called collectCustomizationMigrationHint() inside the Promise.all awaited in Step 2 of sendRequest, before invokeAgent. That helper awaited CustomizationMigrationService.computeMigrationHint. computeMigrationHint fans out across user-data, prompt-file, configured-location, and optional MCP migrations; the first three issue six listPromptFiles calls over three prompt types, whose cold implementation searches user/workspace filesystem locations, then asks the harness for source folders. The agent-host provider waits for asynchronous session customization state; its own comment states that 'the chat request path blocks on this before sending the user's message.' The MCP branch can additionally wait for support discovery and read files while creating a migration plan. Deleted tests prove frequency: Always mode produced three computations for three eligible requests, while Once produced one per session. This PR removes the helper and its awaited Promise.all entry entirely.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send a message in an agent-host chat session while the response migration hint is enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before the PR, sendRequest created the visible request, then awaited hooks, automatic instructions, and collectCustomizationMigrationHint together before participant detection, extension activation, MCP autostart, and invokeAgent. The migration branch therefore delayed message delivery to the agent. After the PR, only hooks and automatic instructions remain in that await; migration assessment is absent from the response path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt, agent, and instruction files across configured user and workspace locations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The removed computation issued six listPromptFiles calls across three unique prompt types. On a warm initialized cache these collapse to three cached type results; cold or uncached discovery searches user and local sources for each effective type and scales with configured roots and matching files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base revision performed this discovery for every eligible request in Always mode and the first request of each session in Once mode; the PR removes those calls from sendRequest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Before the PR this work was awaited before invokeAgent, so the slowest cold discovery delayed time to agent response. It is no longer on this request path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for the first agent-host customization-state snapshot before deriving migration destination folders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Potentially several source-folder queries per migration assessment, but all callers for one subscription share one memoized readiness wait/deadline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base revision reached this wait through computeMigrationHint; the changed revision does not.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The repository explicitly documents that this wait blocked the chat request before sending the user's message. The PR removes the request-path wait.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optionally wait for MCP support discovery and read MCP configuration files to construct a migration plan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One optional MCP assessment per hint computation when MCP migration is enabled; file work scales with active roots and MCP source configurations/candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Eligible Always-mode requests recomputed this assessment per request; the PR performs zero such assessments from sendRequest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously part of the awaited migration-hint branch before invokeAgent; removed from the response path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Collect hook files and automatic instruction context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One hooks collector and at most one automatic-instruction collector per request, with their internal existing caches/grouping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same collectors and placement existed before; only the third migration-hint branch was removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Still awaited before agent invocation and unchanged by the PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One invocation per ordinary agent request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same invocation occurred after migration-hint assessment; its count is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This remains the main response boundary. The PR allows it to begin without waiting for migration assessment.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Request count in Always mode or session count in Once mode, multiplied by configured prompt roots/files and optional MCP roots/configurations. Deleted tests establish three computations for three eligible Always-mode requests and one computation for a Once-mode session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The outer context collectors run concurrently through Promise.all, but progress waits for the slowest branch. The removed hint branch itself launched four migration categories concurrently. Its six prompt-list API calls cover three unique prompt types and may coalesce by per-type promise when prompt locator events have initialized; harness readiness calls share one memoized per-subscription deadline. Requests themselves still follow the existing per-session request scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt locations use per-type cached promises after locator events are initialized and invalidate on file updates; repeated calls can therefore be warm, though the old code still invoked and awaited the migration pipeline. Agent-host customization readiness is memoized per subscription. The old Once mode used session input state as a positive 'shown' cache, while Always deliberately recomputed per request. The PR removes all response-path migration-hint cache states and computations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High. The deleted awaited call, transitive filesystem/protocol implementations, explicit repository comment about blocking message send, and deleted frequency tests directly establish the mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depended on experiment assignment, enabled migration categories, cache warmth, filesystem/provider speed, and whether an agent-host snapshot was already available. The blocking placement and repeated-call mechanism are certain; only elapsed duration and affected population are uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression. The PR removes repeated boundary work from the chat-send critical path and was recorded as a regression fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show the standalone chat customization migration notice as active session/customizations change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The notice's unchanged refresh method awaits computeMigrationHint before updating notice availability. This work affects notice rendering, not agent invocation, and remains cancellation-aware.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt customizations and optionally plan MCP migration for the notice.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One computation per relevant reactive refresh, not per chat response; effective file discovery is reduced by per-type prompt caches on warm runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical before and after this PR; the response hint removal does not move or duplicate this notice computation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks only availability/content of the notice, not chat message delivery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Observe/wait for agent-host customization state used by the notice assessment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Shared per-subscription readiness wait across folder queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can delay the notice refresh but is off the chat-response critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of session/customization context changes and number of configured customization roots/files, not number of chat responses after this PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One refresh is started by the notice's reactive context; disposal/context replacement cancels obsolete work. Inside computeMigrationHint the same four migration categories run concurrently, with prompt cache and shared readiness behavior described above.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt discovery caches by prompt type when initialized and invalidates on locator changes; agent-host readiness is shared per subscription. Notice refreshes are canceled when their owning context is disposed. There is no newly introduced cache or retention.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the path remains separate and unchanged, based on the notice implementation and removed sendRequest call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency of reactive notice refreshes and cache warmth varies, but this path is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the existing notice assessment remains, but the diff neither increases its frequency nor moves it onto a hotter path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench configuration registration and ChatService construction
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Startup registers chat configuration metadata, and ChatService is instantiated when chat is used. The PR removes one experimental setting and two constructor service dependencies.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant per workbench/configuration registration and ChatService instance, independent of request history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new scheduling or fan-out is introduced. Removing injected migration services can only avoid or defer their construction from this consumer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior is added or invalidated. Existing delayed singleton registration for the migration service remains for its other consumers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the import, configuration, and constructor deletions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Instantiation savings are likely small and were not measured; there is no plausible degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; startup/instantiation work is reduced or unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. No diff-introduced performance finding was found. The production change removes an experimentally gated, repeated migration assessment from the pre-agent request critical path; its introducing commit was recorded through report_regression_fix.
